name: Glymphatic sleep headband
subtitle: a sleep band boosting the brain's nightly rinse

effects.effect: during deep sleep the brain flushes out waste through fluid channels
tiny repeated structures bend light, sound or radio the 'wrong' way

effect: during deep sleep the brain flushes out waste through fluid channels
how: The sticky proteins behind Alzheimer's build up as the brain's nightly flush slows with age. When scalp electrodes sense deep sleep, the band sends gentle ultrasound through a thin patterned lens that undoes the skull's distortion, pulsing the brain's fluid channels so more waste washes out.
obstacle: No one knows yet whether a faster flush in people actually slows dementia, and the dose that helps mice may not carry over.
why: Ultrasound speeds brain clearance in mice; nothing wearable has been tried in people.
real: A UCSF pilot trial (NCT07866768) is testing a wearable focused-ultrasound device for glymphatic clearance, and wearable glymphatic monitors exist, but no closed-loop sleep-triggered system with a skull-correcting lens has been demonstrated.
